citation: Seo, Jungryul, Teemu H. Laine, and Kyung-Ah Sohn. "Machine Learning Approaches for Boredom Classification Using EEG." Journal of Ambient Intelligence and Humanized Computing 10 (2019): 3831-3846. https://doi.org/10.1007/s12652-019-01196-3.
discipline: biomedical signal processing and machine learning applied to emotion/boredom recognition, for affective-computing and educational-technology applications
thesis: Of 26 prior EEG emotion-classification studies reviewed, only three (Shen et al. 2009; Katahira et al. 2018; Kim et al. 2018) targeted boredom, and none produced a validated, multi-participant classification model with a reported accuracy. To close this gap, the authors collect EEG from 28 Korean adults via a two-electrode consumer headband (Muse) during video stimuli designed to evoke boredom and non-boredom, extract five feature families (ABP, NABP, DE, DASM, RASM), and train k-NN, MLP, and random forest classifiers with 10-fold cross-validation. Their best result, 86.73% accuracy using k-NN, is framed as demonstrating that boredom classification is feasible from a low-cost, wearable two-electrode sensor rather than research-grade, high-electrode-count EEG. Note: the abstract additionally claims SVM was trained, but the Methods/Results sections report only k-NN, MLP, and RF -- a genuine internal inconsistency in the published article.

sections.title: Abstract, keywords
sections.summary: States the classification task, 28-participant sample, five feature types, three algorithms (as later reported: k-NN, MLP, RF -- though the abstract itself also names SVM), 10-fold cross-validation, and the 86.73% k-NN result.

sections.title: 1 Introduction
sections.summary: Motivates EEG-based emotion recognition generally; argues boredom's educational relevance (Kanevsky 1994; Oroujlou & Vahedi 2011; Yeager et al. 2014 on boredom's negative learning effects); reviews prior non-EEG boredom-detection studies (Mandryk & Atkins 2007; Shen et al. 2009; Jaques et al. 2014; Kim et al. 2018) before narrowing to the EEG-specific gap: only 3 of 26 reviewed EEG-emotion studies targeted boredom.

sections.title: 2 Background -- 2.1 Boredom
sections.summary: Emotion modeling via Russell's (1980) circumplex model, placing boredom in the third quadrant (low arousal, low valence); reviews trait (Fahlman et al. 2013) vs. state (Eastwood et al. 2012) definitions of boredom, explicitly adopting the state view; cites Vogel-Walcutt et al.'s (2012) 37-definition survey and Eastwood et al.'s (2012) three-part attentional definition of boredom.

sections.title: 2.2 Related work
sections.summary: Structured review of 26 prior EEG emotion-classification studies (2001-2018) across participants (2.2.1), electrode counts (2.2.2, Table 2), auxiliary physiological data sources (2.2.3), target emotions (2.2.4, Table 3), feature-extraction methods (2.2.5), frequency-band definitions (2.2.6, Table 4), and models/accuracies (2.2.7, Tables 5-6).

sections.title: 3 Methodology
sections.summary: Participants (3.1, N=28); the Muse EEG sensor (3.2, 4 electrodes, only FP1/FP2 usable); the video-stimulus protocol (3.3); the custom .NET/C# data-collection system (3.4); feature extraction (3.5: ABP, NABP, DE, DASM, RASM); classification models (3.6: k-NN, MLP, RF via Weka).

sections.title: 4 Results
sections.summary: Questionnaire results (4.1, weak/strong boredom dichotomization); watching-time variability (4.2, 7.3-287.9s range); window-size ablation (4.3, 1s/0.5s/0.1s, overfitting at smaller windows); Wrapper Subset Evaluator feature refinement (4.4, gamma/beta informative, theta uninformative); final model evaluation (4.5, Table 9, best k-NN 86.73%).

sections.title: 5 Discussion
sections.summary: Interprets small-window overfitting; situates the gamma/beta finding against Katahira et al.'s (2018) flow-state theta/beta findings; argues three novelty claims relative to Shen et al. (2009) and Kim et al. (2018): larger sample, validated cross-validation, and a two-electrode wearable sensor (usability/accuracy trade-off vs. Lin et al. 2009's 92.57% with 30+ electrodes).

sections.title: 6 Conclusion
sections.summary: Restates the 86.73% k-NN result; proposes future work fusing the already-collected but unanalyzed GSR data with EEG, and addressing k-NN's residual overfitting risk.

sections.title: Acknowledgements and References
sections.summary: Funding: Korea MSIT/ITRC (IITP-2018-2018-0-01431); acknowledges University of Eastern Finland collaborators; ~65 references.

constructs.label: situational vs. trait/state boredom
constructs.treatment: explicitly adopted: 'This study treats boredom as a state of emotion,' against Fahlman et al.'s (2013) trait view

constructs.label: boredom proneness
constructs.treatment: not measured; cited only as the trait pole set aside by the study's state-boredom framing

constructs.label: attentional disengagement / meta-awareness
constructs.treatment: Eastwood et al.'s (2012) three-part attentional definition of boredom is reviewed as one of several surveyed accounts, but the authors' own operational grounding is Russell's arousal/valence circumplex placement plus physiological-change detection, not an attention-failure construct

constructs.label: flow / engagement (contrast pole)
constructs.treatment: treated only via citation of Katahira et al. (2018), whose frontal-theta-during-flow finding is used as interpretive support for the study's own theta-band result; flow is not itself measured by Seo et al.

constructs.label: monotony / meaninglessness
constructs.treatment: operationalized without being named: the boredom-evoking stimulus (a small circle tracing a larger circle's boundary at constant slow speed, looping until manually stopped) is a de facto monotony induction

constructs.label: temporality of boredom (time-drag)
constructs.treatment: cited only, via Fahlman et al.'s manifestation 'experiencing a slow passage of time'; not independently developed or measured

constructs.label: boredom-as-regulatory-signal (functional account)
constructs.treatment: not treated; boredom is framed purely as a classification target for adaptive systems, never theorized as having adaptive/regulatory value

constructs.label: mind-wandering / task-unrelated thought
constructs.treatment: not treated; the term and comparable constructs never appear in the source

constructs.label: profound/deep boredom (FCM 3rd form)
constructs.treatment: not treated; purely empirical biomedical-signal article, Heidegger never cited

constructs.label: being-bored-by (1st form) / being-bored-with (2nd form)
constructs.treatment: not treated; no phenomenological vocabulary appears anywhere in the source

measures.label: EEG alpha/theta power
measures.signal: alpha (7.5-13 Hz) and theta (4-8 Hz) sub-bands within ABP/NABP
measures.apparatus: Muse headband, FP1/FP2, 10 Hz band-power sampling
measures.key_result: theta-band features were never selected as meaningful by the Wrapper Subset Evaluator (WSE); alpha was also comparatively weak; read as convergent with Katahira et al.'s (2018) finding of strong frontal theta during flow (boredom's functional opposite)

measures.label: EEG frontal alpha asymmetry
measures.signal: differential asymmetry (DASM) and rational asymmetry (RASM), computed per frequency band (including alpha) from FP1-FP2 differential entropy
measures.apparatus: Muse headband, FP1/FP2; grounded in Davidson & Fox (1982) and Davidson (1992) frontal-asymmetry-and-emotion theory
measures.key_result: DASM and RASM (along with plain DE) were rarely selected by WSE -- underperforming for boredom classification specifically, in tension with their prominence in the general emotion-EEG literature (e.g., Zheng et al. 2017)

measures.label: EEG functional connectivity
measures.apparatus: structurally precluded -- Zheng et al.'s (2017) vertical-symmetry connectivity-adjacent features require more than two electrode pairs, unavailable with this study's two-electrode (FP1/FP2) montage

measures.label: EEG eyes-open vs. eyes-closed
measures.key_result: protocol is continuous eyes-open video viewing throughout; no eyes-closed condition

measures.label: heart rate / HRV
measures.apparatus: galvanic skin response (GSR) collected via Grove GSR sensor + Arduino as a related autonomic channel, but explicitly not analyzed in this study
measures.key_result: reserved for future work (proposed EEG+GSR fusion in Conclusion); no heart-rate sensor was used at all

measures.label: self-report / survey scale
measures.signal: 5-point Likert boredom-intensity item (None/Little/Somewhat/Much/Very Much) administered after each video stage
measures.apparatus: questionnaire, paper/digital administration not specified beyond Likert format
measures.key_result: dichotomized into weak-boredom (30 of 56 answers) and strong-boredom (28 of 56 answers) groups, which supplied ground-truth class labels for every classifier -- not the raw EEG signal

measures.label: behavioral (RT / errors / performance-monitoring)
measures.apparatus: n/a -- passive video-watching paradigm with no task or reaction-time component

measures.label: predictive-processing model
measures.key_result: no predictive-coding or predictive-processing theoretical framework is invoked anywhere in this source

measures.label: pupil dilation / pupillometry
measures.apparatus: n/a -- no eye-tracking apparatus of any kind in this study (contrast with sibling unit bor-sec-28, Kim, Seo & Laine 2018, which pairs EEG with eye-gaze tracking)

measures.label: ML classification
measures.signal: 40 base features (ABP 10, NABP 10, DE 10, DASM 5, RASM 5) across k-NN, MLP, and RF classifiers; WSE-based feature-subset refinement
measures.apparatus: Weka software (Hall et al. 2009); k-NN per Aha et al. (1991), 3 weighting options; MLP per Rosenblatt (1961), 1 hidden layer, 4 node-count formulas; RF per Ho (1995)/Barandiaran (1998), Weka defaults; 10-fold cross-validation throughout; 1-second analysis window (chosen over 0.5s/0.1s to avoid overfitting)
measures.key_result: best result: k-NN, '1/distance' weighting, WSE-refined '10-2' feature subset, 1s window -- 86.73% accuracy, an 11.2-percentage-point gain over the unrefined 40-feature baseline (75.51%); MLP and RF each peaked at 78.57% accuracy (AUC 0.858 and 0.866 respectively, feature group '10-6'). Note: the abstract's claim of also training an SVM classifier is unsupported by the Methods/Results, which report only k-NN, MLP, and RF.

readings.claim: Of 26 prior EEG emotion-classification studies reviewed (2001-2018), only Shen et al. (2009) and Kim et al. (2018) targeted boredom as a classification objective, and neither produced a validated, adequately powered classification model; a third boredom-adjacent study, Katahira et al. (2018), examined EEG correlates of flow (compared against boredom) but likewise produced no classifier.
k-NN with WSE-refined features and '1/distance' weighting achieved the study's best result: 86.73% accuracy at a one-second window with 10-fold cross-validation.
Feature refinement via the Wrapper Subset Evaluator improved k-NN accuracy by 11.2 percentage points over the unrefined 40-feature baseline.

Gamma-band features were the most informative for boredom classification specifically; theta-band features were never selected as meaningful; beta was selected less often than gamma; frontal-asymmetry features (DASM, RASM) and differential entropy (DE) were rarely selected, in tension with their prominence in the broader emotion-EEG literature.

Smaller analysis windows (0.5s, 0.1s) produced substantially higher raw accuracy, but this reflects overfitting from near-identical adjacent samples split across cross-validation folds rather than genuine signal; the authors deliberately report the 1-second window despite its lower raw accuracy.

The study improves on prior boredom-EEG work via a substantially larger sample than Shen et al. (2009)'s single participant, validated 10-fold cross-validation unlike Shen et al.'s unreported method, and a two-electrode wearable sensor traded against Lin et al. (2009)'s 92.57% accuracy with 30+ electrodes for a favorable usability/accuracy balance.

The abstract states that support vector machine, random forest, and k-nearest neighbors were the three trained algorithms, but the Methodology and Results sections (3.6, 4.5, Tables 8-9) explain and report only k-NN, MLP, and RF -- SVM is never trained, tuned, or reported.
readings.stance: internal inconsistency (our observation of the source, not a claim it makes about itself)

readings.claim: Future work should combine the already-collected but unanalyzed GSR data with EEG to seek higher classification accuracy, and investigate approaches for reducing k-NN's residual overfitting risk.

interlocutors.name: Kim, Joochan, Seo, Jungryul, & Laine, Teemu H. (2018)
interlocutors.role: Companion study (shared authorship, bor-sec-28 in this cluster); source of the boredom-evoking rotating-circle video stimulus reused here; found an EEG-eye gaze correlation during boredom but provided no classification model or accuracy figure -- explicitly positioned as one of the two studies this paper claims to improve upon

interlocutors.name: Shen, Longfei, Wang, Minjuan, & Shen, Ronghuai (2009)
interlocutors.role: Only other EEG-based boredom-targeting study among the 26 reviewed; single participant, brain+blood+skin+heart signals, no clearly reported validation method; directly compared against and claimed to be improved upon

interlocutors.name: Katahira, Kentaro, et al. (2018)
interlocutors.role: 'EEG correlates of the flow state'; found strong frontal theta and greater beta amplitude during boredom's functional opposite (flow); used as convergent interpretive support for this study's gamma/beta feature-selection finding, though via a different task (mental arithmetic)

interlocutors.name: Zheng, Wei-Long, Zhu, Jia-Yi, & Lu, Bao-Liang (2017)
interlocutors.role: Source of the DE/DASM/RASM feature methodology (62-electrode sensor); partially adopted here, but vertical/horizontal-symmetry connectivity-adjacent features could not be used given only two electrodes

interlocutors.name: Davidson, Richard J., & Fox, Nathan A. (1982); Davidson, Richard J. (1992)
interlocutors.role: Frontal EEG asymmetry-and-emotion theory grounding the DASM/RASM feature rationale

interlocutors.name: Russell, James A. (1980)
interlocutors.role: Circumplex model of affect; adopted as the study's emotion-modeling framework, placing boredom in the low-arousal/low-valence third quadrant

interlocutors.name: Eastwood, John D., Frischen, A., Fenske, M.J., & Smilek, D. (2012)
interlocutors.role: State-boredom / attentional definition of boredom, reviewed as one of several definitions; source of the study's adopted state (vs. trait) framing

interlocutors.name: Vogel-Walcutt, Jennifer J., et al. (2012)
interlocutors.role: 37-definition review of state boredom; grounds a low-arousal definition of boredom that the authors note is consistent with Russell's circumplex placement

interlocutors.name: Fahlman, Shelley A., Mercer-Lynn, K.B., Flora, D.B., & Eastwood, J.D. (2013)
interlocutors.role: Multidimensional State Boredom Scale; representative of the trait view of boredom the study sets aside; source of the five-part boredom-manifestation typology including 'slow passage of time'

interlocutors.name: Lin, Yuan-Pin, et al. (2009, 2008, 2010)
interlocutors.role: Highest-accuracy comparator (92.57%) using 30+ electrodes for music-emotion classification; benchmark for the electrode-count/accuracy/usability trade-off discussion

interlocutors.name: Kanevsky, Lannie S. (1994); Oroujlou, N. & Vahedi, M. (2011); Yeager, David S., et al. (2014)
interlocutors.role: Cited in the Introduction to motivate boredom's negative educational impact and the applied rationale for automatic boredom detection in learning technology

interlocutors.name: Hall, Mark, et al. (2009)
interlocutors.role: Weka data-mining software used for all classifier training/evaluation

interlocutors.name: Aha, David W., Kibler, D., & Albert, M.K. (1991)
interlocutors.role: Instance-based learning algorithm underlying Weka's k-NN (IBk) implementation

interlocutors.name: Rosenblatt, Frank (1961)
interlocutors.role: Perceptron/neural-network origin underlying the MLP classifier

interlocutors.name: Ho, Tin Kam (1995); Barandiaran, I. (1998)
interlocutors.role: Random forest / random subspace method origin underlying the RF classifier

tensions.axis: gamma/beta-band informativeness for boredom (Seo et al.'s finding) vs. frontal-asymmetry/alpha-centered feature paradigm dominant in the general emotion-EEG literature (e.g., Zheng et al. 2017)
tensions.note: Seo et al.'s WSE feature-refinement results found DASM, RASM, and DE -- all grounded in frontal-asymmetry theory -- rarely selected as informative for boredom classification specifically, in tension with their widespread use for emotion classification generally; gamma and beta bands proved more discriminative in this dataset.

tensions.axis: electrode count vs. classification accuracy and usability
tensions.note: Lin et al. (2009) achieved higher accuracy (92.57%) with 30+ electrodes for a different classification task; Seo et al. achieve 86.73% with only two electrodes and frame this as a favorable usability trade-off rather than a performance deficit.

tensions.axis: raw window-size accuracy vs. genuine generalizable signal
tensions.note: Smaller analysis windows (0.5s, 0.1s) yield much higher raw accuracy and AUC, but the authors interpret this as an overfitting artifact from near-identical adjacent samples rather than a genuine effect, and deliberately report the lower-accuracy 1-second window as their real result.

tensions.axis: methodological rigor of this study vs. prior boredom-EEG studies
tensions.note: Seo et al. position their validated 10-fold cross-validation and 28-participant sample against Shen et al.'s (2009) single-participant, unvalidated design and Kim et al.'s (2018) correlational-only (no classifier, no accuracy) approach.

tensions.axis: abstract's stated methodology (SVM, RF, k-NN) vs. the Methods/Results sections' actual methodology (k-NN, MLP, RF)
tensions.note: A genuine internal inconsistency in the published article: SVM is named in the abstract as one of three trained algorithms but is never explained, trained, tuned, or reported in the Methodology or Results sections or in Tables 8-9.

dataset_channels.target: Boredom Experiment (VR Attention Study) -- EEG-based ML boredom classifier channel
dataset_channels.note: Seo et al. is the only source in the currently-built portion of this cluster reporting a validated, cross-validated, multi-participant EEG-based boredom-classification accuracy, and its feature-selection finding (gamma/beta informative; theta/alpha/frontal-asymmetry comparatively uninformative for boredom specifically) is the most direct source-grounded guidance in this corpus for prioritizing spectral features in a future EEG channel. However, the dataset entry does not yet exist, its actual instrumentation is unknown, and this finding derives from a two-electrode consumer sensor during passive video-watching rather than a VR attention task; any linkage to the dataset's real channel design requires independent confirmation (P/anticipatory-application).
